title: SDK lifecycle gateway: triage rubric for polyglot streaming & auth patterns
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Objective: Create and operationalize a lightweight triage & prioritization gateway for incoming SDK/client library requests from customers and internal stakeholders focusing on two recurring axes: (1) polyglot language support gaps and (2) auth/streaming ergonomics for enterprise flows.

Background: Over the last two quarters we've accumulated ~40 discrete asks across English/JS/Python/Go/Java, plus several enterprise customers requesting opinionated auth flows (multi-tenant SSO, key rotation, KMS integration) and streaming ergonomics (client-side reconnect, incremental error semantics, structured streaming events). Current ad-hoc handling leads to long feedback loops and inconsistent shipping criteria. This ticket defines a rubric to triage, categorize, and fast-path small wins while flagging high-risk enterprise work for scoped projects.

Scope: This is a product-level intake/decision asset (triage rubric + runbook + intake form template) rather than engineering implementation. Outputs will be: triage rubric (scoring), categorization buckets, recommended actions per bucket, sample responses/templates, and an initial backlog of 10 prioritized requests with owners.

Success metrics: reduced mean time-to-first-response to customers from 12d -> 3d; 30% of low-effort SDK asks shipped within one sprint; clear signal for Dedicated/Private lift requests to trigger enterprise scoping.
acceptance_criteria: A documented triage rubric published to Confluence with scoring on impact, effort, security, and customer contractual risk
An intake form (Google/Form or internal tool) that normalizes request metadata (language, auth, streaming, customer tier, example code)
A first-pass prioritized backlog of >=10 requests with owners and recommended action (e.g., quick patch, RFC, enterprise scoping)
Communication templates for PMs/SEs to respond to requesters with estimated timelines
Routing rules for 'enterprise-high' signals that create a scoped project (release + SOW path)

2026-03-03 Design (Anya Singh): Proposed UX patterns for streaming ergonomics — reconnect/backpressure API, explicit chunk/metadata envelope, and unified event types for client libs. Will prototype TS/py examples.
